# Final whole-course editorial verification

**Pass. Chapter 6 resolves WC-01 on `c2f9cb211de7e204e08920b8cf3d164d7195b866`.** The clean worktree and locally served build manifest identified that revision. I compared all 47 generated files with `206828b`. Of 35 HTML pages, 34 matched byte for byte. Replacing one figure sentence in the earlier Chapter 6 reproduced the entire final page. The only other difference was the revision and timestamp in the manifest. [Assignment](../tasks.json) · [Build comparison](build-delta.json)

I followed the Lab link to the corrected figure. Each scenario repeats eight phase slots, admits two north–south and two east–west vehicles per cycle, and carries both queues into cycle two. My independent replay matched the recorded results available without JavaScript for both scenarios. Original B ends slot 8 with two north–south vehicles waiting. Slot 9 admits two east–west vehicles and serves one of the waiting north–south vehicles. Applying the chapter’s separate mean-wait procedure, I stopped admissions after slot 16. Both queues emptied in slot 18, giving 44 vehicle-slots divided by eight arrivals, or 5.5 slots per vehicle. [Model and boundary checks](check-90b.md)

Chapter 5 saves the edited B separately and hands original B to Chapter 6. Its slot-9 departure explains the first quiz answer. The other two ask what would qualify the spreadsheet’s count of 20 and how to time a loaded interface. Chapter 7 uses the original rows and boundary departure as acceptance checks. I inspected all nine answer explanations in the served page. The delivery owner exercised all nine options in Chrome. [Browser observations](browser-candidate.json)

The ordered review of fourteen chapters and the companion carries forward, including its judgments on physical evidence, release decisions and investment. This verdict covers the local candidate. Public deployment requires separate evidence. The study records zero human sessions, so transfer to another problem and the effect of the longest-answer cue remain unmeasured.
